reminderWelcomeBody: Food diversification starts gently from 4 months. Read the guide to get your bearings, then log baby’s first food.
reminderStage6Title: Baby is 6 months old: time for proteins
reminderStage6Body: It’s time to introduce meat, fish, well-cooked egg and legumes for iron. If not done yet, this is also the key window for allergens (egg, peanut, gluten…).
reminderStage9Title: Baby is 9 months old: first pieces
reminderStage9Body: Baby picks up food between thumb and index finger. Offer sticks of cooked vegetables, slices of avocado, well-cooked pasta. Always under supervision.
reminderStage12Title: Baby is 1 year old: adapted family meals
reminderStage12Body: Baby gradually shares family meals, in adapted versions: less salty, less sweet, cut-up pieces. Milk stays at ~500 mL/day.
reminderStaleDiversityBody: Get back into the rhythm: offer a food not yet tried. Variety keeps taste curiosity and allergen tolerance going.
reminderPendingAllergenBody: The longer you wait, the higher the allergy risk. Introduce it in a form suited to baby’s age.
reminderHighRiskWindowBody: This is the key period to introduce peanut, egg, milk, gluten… Delaying does not protect: quite the opposite (LEAP, EAT).
reminderRepeatExposureBody: Taste acceptance is built through repetition: up to 10 times for some foods. The same goes for maintaining allergen tolerance.
reminderCategoryImbalanceBody: More than {percent}% of your entries over the last 14 days are in the “{category}” category. Diversify with other groups (proteins, starches, fruits…).
reminderMaintainAllergenBody: Baby has not had {allergen} for {days} days. Ideally offer it 2 to 3 times a week to maintain tolerance.

landingFaqQ1: When should I start weaning my baby?
landingFaqA1: French guidance (HCSP 2020, Santé publique France) and European guidance (ESPGHAN 2017) align: weaning starts between 4 and 6 completed months, never before 4 months (17 weeks), ideally before 6 months to take advantage of the allergen introduction window.
landingFaqQ2: Which allergens should be introduced early?
landingFaqA2: HCSP 2020 and the LEAP (2015) and EAT (2016) studies recommend early introduction (from 4 to 6 months) for: egg, peanut, cow's milk, gluten (wheat), fish, tree nuts (as a purée), sesame. The app tracks 12 allergens in total (reference: EU regulation 1169/2011 on labelling, minus lupin and sulphites); the others (crustaceans, molluscs, celery, mustard) are tracked for journal completeness. Soy is not on the early-introduction list: HCSP and ANSES advise against soy-based products before age 3.
landingFaqQ3: Do I have to choose between purées and baby-led weaning?
landingFaqA3: No. The French Society of Paediatrics recognises baby-led weaning, classic purées, and a mixed approach as valid. What matters is adapting texture to age, watching for choking signs, and offering a varied diet.
landingFaqQ4: Which foods to avoid before age 1 and before age 3?
landingFaqA4: Before age 1: honey (botulism), plain cow's milk as a drink, added salt, added sugar, fruit juice. Before age 3: risky raw foods (raw eggs, raw meat or fish), hard and round foods (peanuts, whole grapes), sugary and artificially sweetened drinks.
landingFaqA5: Yes. Diversif is open source, self-hosted, free, and ad-free. Your data stays on your own server or host.

guideSeoTitle: Complementary feeding guide: babies from 4 months to 3 years · Diversif
guideSeoDescription: A sourced, comprehensive guide: 10 golden rules, 4 age-based stages, the 12 priority allergens, textures, foods to avoid, and how to handle allergic reactions. Sources: HCSP, Santé publique France, ESPGHAN, WHO, the LEAP and EAT studies.
aideWhatBody: Diversif helps you through your baby’s food diversification: log every food you offer, track the 12 major allergens, vary tastes and textures, and keep a record of reactions. The app is self-hosted and ad-free — your data stays with you.
aideSharingBody: Tracking is meant to be shared. From your Profile, open the child’s settings and generate an invite code, then send the link to the other parent. Once they’ve created an account and accepted the invitation, you both see the same log and can each record meals and reactions. The code expires after 7 days and can be used only once.
aideTrustBody: The guidance draws on authoritative sources: HCSP, Santé publique France, ANSES, ESPGHAN, WHO, the French Paediatric Society, and the LEAP and EAT studies.
aideSeoDescription: How Diversif works, how to share tracking with the other parent, and why you can trust its guidance.
